posts.name: Theta_Sigma
posts.cooked:
Most games, unless they have an online requirement, can be played offline. In fact, if you don't have a connection, you can log in in offline mode, and access any games you have already installed that don't require you to be online and play them

A Steam account can be logged into by one machine at a time, though it is easy enough to log into an account on one computer, start a game, log out of Steam and log in on another computer.

If you opt into the beta, you can do things like Family Share and streaming, but it's not necessary (and your Steam client updates pretty much every day with more bug fixes.).

 

If the game has a purely offline mode (like it is now), there would be no requirement for you to be online, except for the original installation.

posts.name: bluedarky
posts.cooked:
xThe Killswitch:

I realize this isn't a top priority right now, but are there plans on improving the soundtrack a bit? It would be really awesome to include character-specific themes. For example: selecting Bunker would result in a heavy metal theme, Legacy has a Superman-esque anthem, and Visionary has a Sci-Fi tone to her theme (Twilight Zone/Dr. Who). Just a thought.

As much as I like the suggestion there are a few issues with this idea.

First is the fact that they have to design another 50+ soundtracks to do this and make each distinctly unique for each character and environment, then you have copyright and trademark issues to take into account, from your post alone any superman-esque theme runs the risk of sounding close enough to any one of the hundreds of Superman themes to count as an infringement.

Second is the question of where to play these tracks, during each players turn?  What about poor Legacy, in comparision to Tachyon most of Legacy's turns are over too quickly for the theme to be heard.  And when we get online multiplayer, what do we do about someone who purposely draws out their turns because they like the theme.  And picking a random one for the entire match can result in people dropping out because they dislike the theme chosen.

Right now with the theme being chosen by the Environment we're in a sweet spot of design and game cohesion.  For the design perspective it means that they only need to make 2 themes per expansion, for the game cohesion it means that you know what the music will be going into the match, and it helps the environment (especially ones like The Block, Silver Gulch and MDP where they spend most of the game either fighting each other or doing nothing) have a greater impact on the game.

Another idea I had was maybe having a "test" or "practice/training" mode, where you could stack the deck how you wanted, and being able to play out any scenario you saw fit (provided you could actually legally pull it off; for example, you couldn't play two limited cards of the same name). posts.cooked:
Just played my first game - just did one I knew should be fairly quick and easy, so it was Legacy, Ra, and Wraith versus Baron Blade in Insula Primalis (volcano came out in the second round, right after Ra had played Flesh of th Sun God so that kind of helped ;)). I have some feedback :).

~ Creating a desktop shortcut doesn't seem to work - it does create a shortcut (which is an image of a globe, which seemed a bit odd to me as I'd've thought it'd be a picture of Blade's face or an SC logo or something) but then I just get an error when I try to use it, saying the shortcut properties are wrong or something. I had to run the game by opening my Steam window and accessing it from within my library.

~ The way the cards flash to show which ones you can play I found kind of irritating as I was trying to look at the cards and the constant glowy thing was distracting.

~ There seems no way to change the order in which the cards are laid out (either in-hand or in play) - I like to switch around my cards to have all the ongoings together, for example. Also, I like to stack multiple copies of the same card on top of each other in order to save space (so in this game I had three copies of Stun Bolt in-hand taking up three cards' worth of space when they could easily just be in a pile with the top of the lower cards sticking out so you can see how many you have). It makes it feel more restricted and less like a proper "virtual tabletop".

~ It would be nice if you could make the play areas resizeable or something, to save having to scroll back and forth along your hand when deciding what to play. I can see that being a pain if you're playing a hero who ends up with a big hand or a lot of stuff in play (someone like the Adept or Omni-10, even if many of the latter's cards go off automatically).

~ It felt like there was a lot of unnecessary mouse movement, having to go halfway across the screen to confirm various card activities and stuff. But maybe there are hotkeys or something - I haven't looked into that.

I forgot to check whether you can look at other heroes' hands/play areas when trying to decide what to play on your current hero. I'll try and remember to do that next time ;). But all in all, it wasn't bad and I was able to mostly follow what was going on (though I failed to spot whether Stealth was actually soaking damage since I didn't notice it in the damage report message...maybe I didn't read it before it disappeared though). Also, these are just the things that stood out to me the most after one short game, so don't think that I only have grumpy, moany things to say ;). I'm just used to tabletop, that's all, and it felt weird not keeping track of all the things that were going on (damage buffs, etc) because the computer was doing that for me.

If they release the mini expansions alongside Eternal Haka.

Well so far the promos released, three out of the four don't have a major story arc as to why they're around, Rook City Wraith, despite the name, is just Wraith in her day job away from the Freedom Five, Super Scientific Tachyon is the same and G.I. Bunker is the WWII version of Bunker.  As a result these are unlocked through just playing the hero, abet unnaturally to some experienced players.

Young Legacy on the other hand is directly tied into the storyline, she went to Mars with her father and picked up the mantle full time after Baron Blade killed Paul Parsons (at least in one timeline before Shattered Timelines screwed everything).

Onto the other promos, it's reasonable to assume that team promos (Freedom Six, Dark Watch, Prime Wardens) will be unlocked together, other promos are tied to significant story events (Redeemer Fanatic, Ra Horus of Two Horizons)

Now my reasoning is that Eternal Haka is Haka from The Final Wasteland, it's a minor plot point that Haka has survived beyond any other human ever to live, hell, half the flavor text on the cards from The Final Wasteland is Haka describing the Cryptids.

 

Now I'll admit it would suck if there was a promo tied to a single mini-expansion, but still, it's worth considering even as an alternate method to unlock him.
